subject.title: bug: Duplicate messages sent to Slack

question: Can a maintainer or operator inspect the named Slack session's gateway logs and Slack message IDs to identify the exact duplicate-delivery path?
rationale: Source inspection shows multiple adjacent duplicate guards, but the report cannot be safely closed or scoped to one fix without log-backed proof for the named session.

options.title: Inspect session proof first
options.body: Keep this open until logs, Slack timestamps, and message IDs tie the duplicate to a specific shipped or current-main guard, or to a remaining code path.

options.title: Close only with matching fix proof
options.body: Close later as implemented only if a specific commit or release is shown to cover the same duplicate path observed in the named session.

options.title: Open a narrow fix after proof
options.body: If logs identify an uncovered path, queue a focused Slack delivery regression rather than adding a speculative broad dedupe layer.

recommendation.title: Inspect session proof first
recommendation.body: Keep this open until logs, Slack timestamps, and message IDs tie the duplicate to a specific shipped or current-main guard, or to a remaining code path.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the clearest identified history on shipped Slack duplicate-reply hardening and current main Slack delivery code provenance.
